# Getting started

Load a typed config from a file with `scarab-config-file`. The whole
flow is three steps: define your serde model, pick a
[`Discovery`](/reference/config-port#discovery) spec, load.

## 1. Add the crates

Scarab isn't published to crates.io — depend on the git repo, like
every org consumer does (`myco`, `tarsi`, …):

```toml
[dependencies]
# org consumers pin a rev — see myco/Cargo.toml for the current one
scarab-config = { git = "ssh://git@github.com/9aia/scarab.git" }
scarab-config-file = { git = "ssh://git@github.com/9aia/scarab.git" }
scarab-config-yaml = { git = "ssh://git@github.com/9aia/scarab.git" }
scarab-config-toml = { git = "ssh://git@github.com/9aia/scarab.git" }
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
```

## 2. Define your config model

Scarab stays generic — your repo owns the `Config` type:

```rust
use serde::Deserialize;

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct MyConfig {
    name: String,
    port: u16,
}
```

## 3. Load it

```rust
use scarab_config_file::FileSource;

let cfg: MyConfig = FileSource::for_app("myapp").load()?;
```

`FileSource::for_app("myapp")` wires the org conventions for you:
env var `MYAPP_CONFIG`, search dirs `[".", "~/.config/myapp"]`, and
the standard format pair (YAML preferred, TOML fallback). For `myapp`
it resolves, in order:

1. `$MYAPP_CONFIG` — an explicit file path
2. `./myapp.yaml`, `./myapp.yml`, `./myapp.toml`
3. `~/.config/myapp/myapp.yaml`, `.yml`, `.toml`

The first existing file wins. See [reference: config
port](/reference/config-port) for the full contract and [how-to:
customize discovery](/how-to/customize-config-discovery) for custom
search specs.

## Next steps

* [Layer configs from several files](/how-to/layered-config) — merge
  `~/.config/<name>/` with a project file instead of first-match.
* [Write a template pack](/how-to/write-a-template-pack) — ship
  rendered config files as a tamias `type: template` package.
* [Deploy a template pack](/how-to/deploy-a-template-pack) — the
  driver verbs, variable layers, and uninstall semantics.

# Customize config discovery

`Discovery::for_app` covers the common case. When it doesn't — a
different env var, extra search dirs, a different format set, or an
explicit `--config` path — build the [`FileSource`](/reference/config-port#filesource-t)
directly.

## Custom env var and dirs

```rust
use scarab_config::{Discovery, expand_tilde};
use scarab_config_file::FileSource;

let discovery = Discovery::for_app("myapp")
    .env_var("MYAPP_CFG")                    // override $MYAPP_CONFIG
    .dirs([".", "~/.config/myapp", "/etc/myapp"]);

let src = FileSource::new(discovery);
```

`dirs` entries may contain `~` — expanded via `expand_tilde` at
search time. `.env_var("…")` replaces the env step; `.without_env()`
removes it entirely. `Discovery::bare("myapp")` starts with no env var
and no dirs — fill both yourself.

## Explicit path wins over everything

Set `explicit` on the source (a `--config`-style flag) and it takes
precedence over the env var and all discovery candidates:

```rust
let mut src = FileSource::new(discovery);
src.explicit = Some("/etc/myapp/overrides.toml".into());
```

An explicit path that doesn't exist is an error naming the path — a
named path that misses is a config error, not a silent skip.

## Custom format set or order

`FileSource::new` uses the standard pair — `[YamlFormat,
TomlFormat]`. `with_formats` takes any `Vec<Box<dyn
ConfigFormat<T>>>`; earlier formats win candidate ties within a
directory, and each format's `extensions()` are tried in declared
order. To make TOML preferred:

```rust
use scarab_config_toml::TomlFormat;
use scarab_config_yaml::YamlFormat;

let src = FileSource::with_formats(
    discovery,
    vec![Box::new(TomlFormat), Box::new(YamlFormat)],
);
```

With TOML first, `myapp.toml` beats `myapp.yaml` in the same
directory.

## Extensionless explicit paths

`load_path` dispatches on extension; a path with no extension parses
with the first (preferred) format — the back-compat seam for
`--config` pointing at a suffix-less file. An extension no format
claims is an error: `no config format claims '.json'`.

## Parse a specific file

Skip discovery entirely when the caller already resolved a path:

```rust
let cfg: MyConfig = src.load_path(Path::new("/etc/myapp.toml"))?;
```

## Inject env lookups in tests

`locate_with` / `load_with` take `env: &dyn Fn(&str) ->
Option<String>` so tests never touch the process environment:

```rust
let cfg = src.load_with(&|k| (k == "MYAPP_CONFIG").then(|| "/tmp/x.yaml".into()))?;
```

# Layer configs from several files

`FileSource` picks the *first* matching file — one config wins, the
rest are ignored. `LayeredFileSource` is the merge counterpart: it
collects **one file per search dir**, folds them into a single
`serde_json::Value` tree, applies programmatic overrides, and
deserializes into your model. Use it when a base config (say,
`~/.config/myapp/myapp.yaml`) should be *overridden* by a project or
environment file rather than replaced by it.

## Swap the source

```rust
use scarab_config_file::LayeredFileSource;

// same Discovery conventions as FileSource::for_app
let cfg: MyConfig = LayeredFileSource::for_app("myapp").load()?;
```

Under `Discovery::for_app` the dirs are `[".", "~/.config/myapp"]`
and the **last dir is the base**: `~/.config/myapp/myapp.yaml`
loads first, `./myapp.yaml` merges over it. Within each dir only the
preferred file counts — `myapp.yaml` beats `myapp.yml` beats
`myapp.toml`, and the losers are not merged.

## Precedence, lowest to highest

1. `<dir>/<name>.<ext>` per search dir, last dir first
2. the explicit path / `$<NAME>_CONFIG` file — merged **on top** of
   every dir layer (unlike `FileSource`, where it replaces discovery)
3. `overrides` — flat dotted-path keys, the highest layer

```rust
use scarab_config_file::LayeredFileSource;
use serde_json::json;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

let mut src = LayeredFileSource::<MyConfig>::for_app("myapp");
src.explicit = Some("./deploy/prod.yaml".into()); // top file layer
src.overrides = BTreeMap::from([
    ("server.port".to_string(), json!(8443)),
    ("server.tls.enabled".to_string(), json!(true)),
]);
let cfg = src.load()?;
```

## Merge semantics

Layers merge as `serde_json::Value`, never on your typed model —
`MyConfig` only needs `DeserializeOwned` (no `Serialize`).
`merge_value` does the folding:

* **objects merge key-wise, recursively** — a key the overlay omits
  survives from the base
* **scalars, arrays, and null replace** — arrays never concatenate;
  set `[c]` over `[a, b]` and you get `[c]`

Each layer file must parse to a mapping — a top-level array or
scalar is an error naming the path (`config layer is not a
mapping`). Mixed formats across dirs are fine: a TOML user config
under a YAML project config merges cleanly. A parse error names the
file it came from.

## Inspect the layers

`layer_paths()` returns the resolved layer paths in merge order
(lowest precedence first) — handy for logging what will be merged:

```rust
for p in src.layer_paths()? {
    println!("layer: {}", p.display());
}
```

`parse_layer(path)` parses one file into a `serde_json::Value` if
you need to inspect or transform a layer yourself; `load_with(env)`
takes the same injected env lookup as `FileSource` for tests.

## When not to layer

* You want "one file wins, done" — that's `FileSource`; don't pay
  for a merge you don't need.
* Your model can't round-trip through `serde_json::Value` — e.g. it
  deserializes from a non-self-describing format lossily. The merge
  happens on JSON, so exotic serde attributes (`#[serde(with)]`,
  borrowed data) may not survive the intermediate `Value`.

# Write a template pack

A template pack is a tamias package with `type: template` whose
`tamias.yaml` carries a `template:` table. The
`tamias-driver-template` driver renders each declared `src` through
the engine and writes it at `into`.

## Pack layout

```
repo-bootstrap/
├── tamias.yaml
├── app.toml.tmpl
└── notes.md.tmpl
```

## Manifest

```yaml
name: repo-bootstrap
type: template
version: "0.1.0"

template:
  vars:
    env: dev # defaults — lowest-precedence layer
  files:
    - src: app.toml.tmpl
      into: ./config/app.toml
    - src: notes.md.tmpl
      into: docs/NOTES.md
```

* `template.vars` — flat `name → value` defaults (any JSON value:
  strings, numbers, bools, lists, tables). Overridable per deploy.
* `template.files[]` — `src` is a path inside the pack payload,
  `into` the render target relative to the deploy target dir.

Both `src` and `into` must be safe relative paths: absolute paths,
empty paths, and `..` components are rejected at validation time —
before anything is written.

## Template syntax

The engine is [minijinja](https://github.com/mitsuhiko/minijinja) —
`{{ var }}`, `{% if %}`, `{% for %}`. It is sandboxed: pack templates
are third-party content and cannot reach the filesystem or network.
Undefined variables render as empty.

```jinja
# app.toml.tmpl
env = "{{ env }}"
repo = "{{ repo }}"
user = "{{ user }}"
```

## Inherit from a parent pack

`template.extends` names other template packs by tamias ref — one
bare ref, one `{source, via}` table, or an ordered list (lowest
precedence first). The child renders the parents' files too, with
the child's `into`s and `vars` winning by default:

```yaml
template:
  extends: git:9aia/scarab//libraries/rust-repo
  vars:
    channel: nightly # overrides the parent's "stable" default
  files:
    - src: extra.toml.tmpl
      into: ./extra.toml
```

`tamias install` resolves the ref(s) and materializes the parents'
payloads inside yours — `.scarab-parent/` for one parent,
`.scarab-parents/<i>/` for several (grandparents nest recursively).
The driver renders ancestor-first: parent files write first, yours
last — on an `into` conflict **you win** by default, and the state
digest records your version. `template.merge` tunes the chain
(`vars`/`into` precedence, `max-depth`) — see
[template packs — composition](/reference/template-packs#composition)
for the full contract, including the vendored-parent case
(`.scarab-parent*/` present without `extends`).

## Variable layers

Later layers win:

1. ancestor `template.vars` defaults (extends chain, ancestor-first),
   then this pack's `template.vars`
2. auto vars — `repo` (git remote basename or dir name of the target
   repo) and `user` (`$USER`/`$LOGNAME`)
3. `--config` vars file (JSON / TOML / YAML by extension)
4. `$TEMPLATE_VAR_<NAME>` env vars (lowercased name)
5. trailing `key=value` args

See [deploy a template pack](/how-to/deploy-a-template-pack) for the
full invocation.

## Validate before shipping

`tamias-driver-template install --dir <pack> --name <pkg>` parses the
manifest, checks every `src` exists and compiles, resolves the var
context, and previews the render plan — writing nothing. Run it
against your pack dir before `tamias publish`.

---

---
url: /scarab/how-to/deploy-a-template-pack.md
---
# Deploy a template pack

Template packs deploy through tamias: `tamias install` fetches the
package and dispatches the `type: template` verbs to
`tamias-driver-template`. You can also run the driver binary directly
against a local payload dir.

## Via tamias

```bash
# the shipped example pack — starter configs for a new Rust workspace
tamias install git:9aia/scarab//libraries/rust-repo
```

Tamias calls the driver's `install` verb for validation, then
`deploy` for the actual render+write. `uninstall`/`remove` reverses
it.

## Directly

```bash
tamias-driver-template <verb> --dir <payload> --name <pkg> \
    [--config <vars-file>] [--target <dir>] [--dry-run] [key=value …]
```

| Verb            | What it does                                                                                                    |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `install`       | Validate the pack and preview the render plan. Writes nothing.                                                  |
| `deploy`        | Render each `template.files[]` entry and write it at `into` under the target dir.                               |
| `uninstall`     | Remove files still matching the recorded sha256 digests.                                                        |
| `config-schema` | Print the JSON Schema for the `--config` vars file.                                                             |
| `capabilities`  | Print `{"name": "template", "types": ["template"], "verbs": […], "engine": "minijinja"}` — the discovery probe. |

On an `extends` chain, `install`/`deploy` render every ancestor pack
inside `.scarab-parent/`/`.scarab-parents/` first — the child's
files win on `into` conflicts by default (`template.merge` tunes
it). See
[template packs — composition](/reference/template-packs#composition).

## Choosing the target dir

`deploy`/`uninstall` write relative to, in order:

1. `--target <dir>`
2. `$TEMPLATE_TARGET`
3. the current working directory

## Overriding variables

Vars resolve in layers (later wins): ancestor `template.vars`
defaults (extends chain) → this pack's `template.vars` → auto vars
(`repo`, `user`) → `--config` file → `$TEMPLATE_VAR_<NAME>` env →
`key=value` args.

```bash
# vars file — parsed as JSON/TOML/YAML by extension (default YAML)
tamias-driver-template deploy --dir ./repo-bootstrap --name repo-bootstrap \
    --config prod.yaml --target ~/myrepo

# env + inline overrides
env=prod TEMPLATE_VAR_replicas=3 \
tamias-driver-template deploy --dir ./repo-bootstrap --name repo-bootstrap \
    --target ~/myrepo replicas=5
```

`--dry-run` prints what would be written without touching the target.

## Uninstall semantics

`deploy` records `.scarab-template-state.json` at the target root —
each `into` path mapped to the sha256 of what was written.
`uninstall` deletes only files whose current digest still matches;
files modified since deploy are left in place and reported as kept.
State entries for already-removed files are dropped, and the state
file itself is removed once nothing remains.

# Crates

Generic config + template expertise — ports are traits, format and engine impls are separate crates; consumers plug in their own config model `T` and template pack.

| crate | layer | purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `scarab-config` | port | Config port — ConfigSource\<T>/ConfigFormat generic over the config model, plus the shared file-discovery spec |
| `scarab-template` | port | Template port — TemplateEngine trait + template-pack model (files, var defaults), generic over the render context |
| `scarab-config-file` | adapter | File impl of ConfigSource — discovery (explicit → env → project → user dir) + extension dispatch to ConfigFormat impls |
| `scarab-config-toml` | adapter | TOML impl of ConfigFormat — parse/render any serde config model |
| `scarab-config-yaml` | adapter | YAML impl of ConfigFormat — parse/render any serde config model |
| `scarab-template-minijinja` | adapter | minijinja impl of scarab_template::TemplateEngine — Jinja-style {{ var }} / {% if %} syntax, sandboxed by default |
| `scarab-compose` | engine | Document composition — include/snippet expansion over YAML/TOML/JSON trees into serde_json::Value |
| `scarab-validate` | engine | JSON Schema validation over serde_json::Value — compile once, validate many |
| `tamias-driver-template` | driver | tamias content driver for type: template — renders template-pack files into declared targets at deploy |
| `scarab-testkit` | testkit | Conformance suites + golden fixtures for the scarab config ports — assert\_\* functions any ConfigFormat/ConfigSource impl runs to prove itself |
| `scarab-xtask` | tooling | Repo chores: check / test / coverage / install / package / smoke / site |

---
# Config port

The config plane is two traits plus a search spec, generic over the
config model `T` (`Deserialize + Serialize`). Scarab never names a
consumer's `Config` type.

## `ConfigFormat<T>`

Syntax-level: which extensions a format claims, `parse`/`render`
over serde. Object-safe via a blanket impl — one `TomlFormat` /
`YamlFormat` value serves every model.

```rust
pub trait ConfigFormat<T>: Send + Sync {
    fn extensions(&self) -> &'static [&'static str];
    fn parse(&self, text: &str) -> Result<T, String>;
    fn render(&self, config: &T) -> Result<String, String>;
}
```

| Impl         | Crate                | Claims                        |
| ------------ | -------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `YamlFormat` | `scarab-config-yaml` | `yaml`, `yml` (in that order) |
| `TomlFormat` | `scarab-config-toml` | `toml`                        |

`scarab_config::format_for(path, formats)` returns the format
claiming `path`'s extension, or `None`.

## `ConfigSource<T>`

Source-level: `load() -> Result<T, String>`. Impls compose formats —
`scarab-config-file`'s `FileSource` (first-match) and
`LayeredFileSource` (merge-all) are the file-backed impls; env/remote
sources are new impls of the same trait.

## `Discovery`

The shared search spec every file-backed source uses. Nothing is
hardcoded per app — basename, env var, and dirs are caller-supplied.

| Field     | Meaning                                                                               |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`    | Config file basename — `myco` → `myco.yaml`, `myco.yml`, `myco.toml`                  |
| `env_var` | Env var naming an explicit config file (`$MYCO_CONFIG`); `None` disables the env step |
| `dirs`    | Directories searched in order for `<name>.<ext>`; `~` expands via `expand_tilde`      |

Constructors and builders:

* `Discovery::for_app(name)` — env var `<NAME>_CONFIG` (uppercased),
  dirs `[".", "~/.config/<name>"]`
* `Discovery::bare(name)` — no env var, no dirs
* `.env_var(var)` / `.without_env()` — set or disable the env step
* `.dirs(iter)` — replace search dirs, in order

## `FileSource<T>`

File-backed `ConfigSource`: discovery + extension dispatch over a set
of `ConfigFormat<T>`s.

| Field       | Meaning                                                       |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `discovery` | Where to search                                               |
| `explicit`  | Explicit `--config`-style path; wins over `discovery.env_var` |
| `formats`   | Syntax formats in preference order                            |

Constructors:

* `FileSource::new(discovery)` — standard formats `[Yaml, Toml]`
* `FileSource::with_formats(discovery, formats)` — caller-chosen set/order
* `FileSource::for_app(name)` — `Discovery::for_app` + standard formats
* `FileSource::standard_formats()` — the `[YamlFormat, TomlFormat]` pair

Requires `T: DeserializeOwned + Serialize` for `new`/`for_app` (the
`ConfigSource` impl bound).

## `LayeredFileSource<T>`

The merge counterpart, in `scarab-config-file`. Where `FileSource`
picks the *first* existing file, `LayeredFileSource` collects **one
file per search dir** (same per-dir preference rules), folds them
low→high precedence into a `serde_json::Value` tree, applies
programmatic dotted-path overrides, then deserializes into `T`.
Formats are held as `ConfigFormat<serde_json::Value>` — layers merge
as JSON, so `T` only needs `DeserializeOwned` (no `Serialize`).

| Field       | Meaning                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `discovery` | Where to search — same `Discovery` spec                                                                               |
| `explicit`  | Explicit path — the **top file layer**, merged over all dir layers (unlike `FileSource`, where it replaces discovery) |
| `formats`   | Syntax formats over `serde_json::Value`, in preference order                                                          |
| `overrides` | `BTreeMap<String, Value>` — flat dotted-path keys (`"server.port"`), the highest layer                                |

Constructors mirror `FileSource`: `new(discovery)`, `for_app(name)`,
`with_formats(discovery, formats)`, `standard_formats()`.

Precedence, lowest to highest:

1. `<dir>/<name>.<ext>` per dir, **last dir first** — under
   `Discovery::for_app` (`[".", "~/.config/<name>"]`) the user config
   is the base and `./<name>.yaml` overrides it
2. the explicit path / `$<NAME>_CONFIG` file
3. `overrides` — dotted-path leaf values

Methods: `layer_paths()` / `layer_paths_with(env)` (merge order,
lowest first), `parse_layer(path)` (one file → `Value`; a non-mapping
document is an error), `load()` / `load_with(env)`. Same
`load_with` env-injection seam as `FileSource` for tests. See
[how-to: layered config](/how-to/layered-config) for the merge
semantics and a worked example.

## Merge helpers

Pure functions in `scarab-config` — the half of layered loading that
never touches the filesystem:

* `merge_value(base, overlay)` — recursive JSON merge: objects merge
  key-wise (overlay wins per key, recursing into shared objects);
  scalars, arrays, and null **replace** — arrays never concatenate
* `apply_overrides(base, overrides)` — flat dotted-path keys
  (`"server.port" → 8080`) set leaves, creating intermediate objects;
  a scalar sitting where a path needs to descend is replaced by an
  object. Call after the file layers are merged
* `env_overrides(env, prefix)` — `<PREFIX>_*` env vars → flat
  dotted keys: the suffix lowercases (`__` separates path
  segments), values parse as JSON when possible else stay strings.
  The bare `<PREFIX>` var itself is not an override. Feed the
  result to `apply_overrides` as the highest-precedence layer —
  the generic env-overlay half config ports compose on top of
  file discovery

## Resolution order

`locate` picks the config path:

1. `explicit` path, else `$<NAME>_CONFIG` — a named path that doesn't
   exist is an error (`config file not found: …`), not a silent skip
2. `<dir>/<name>.<ext>` per search dir, in dir order; within a dir,
   formats in preference order and each format's extensions in
   declared order — YAML before TOML by convention

`load` reads the file and dispatches parsing by extension; an
extensionless explicit path parses with the first (preferred) format;
an unclaimed extension errors with `no config format claims '.<ext>'`.

When nothing is found, the error names the app, the claimed
extensions, and the search steps actually configured.

## Path helpers

* `home_dir()` — `$HOME`, else `$USERPROFILE`, else `/`
* `expand_tilde(path)` — `~`/`~/…` expansion; `~user`, relative, and
  absolute paths pass through untouched
* `user_config_dir(name)` — `~/.config/<name>` (tilde expanded at
  search time)

url: /scarab/reference/template-packs.md
---
# Template packs

A template pack is a tamias package with `type: template` whose
`tamias.yaml` carries a `template:` table. The port lives in
`scarab-template` (pure domain — no I/O, no engine specifics); impls
own the syntax.

## Manifest schema

```yaml
name: repo-bootstrap
type: template
version: "0.1.0"

template:
  vars: # optional — flat name → JSON value map
    env: dev
    replicas: 1
  extends: git:9aia/base//libraries/base-pack # optional — parent ref(s)
  merge: # optional — composition rules (defaults shown)
    vars: child-wins    #   child-wins | parent-wins
    into: child-wins    #   child-wins | parent-wins | error
    max-depth: 8        #   ancestor nesting cap (>= 1)
  files: # required, non-empty
    - src: app.toml.tmpl # path inside the pack payload
      into: ./config/app.toml # render target, relative to target dir
```

### `template.vars`

`BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>` — defaults layer, lowest
precedence. Values may be strings, numbers, bools, arrays, or tables;
templates see them as engine-native values.

### `template.files[]`

| Field  | Meaning                                          |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `src`  | Template path inside the payload root            |
| `into` | Render target, relative to the deploy target dir |

`into` must normalize to a non-empty relative path — absolute paths,
`..`, root/prefix components, and empty results are
`TemplateError::UnsafeTarget`. `src` follows the same rule inside the
payload (`TemplateError::UnsafeSource`).

### `template.extends`

Optional parent declaration(s) — one or several tamias refs
(`git:org/repo//path`, `cf:…`, a store name, …). Three spellings,
all normalizing to an ordered parent list **lowest precedence
first**:

```yaml
extends: git:9aia/base//libraries/base-pack            # one parent
# extends: { source: git:9aia/base//x, via: tamias-ref }  # structured
# extends:                                             # several parents
#   - git:9aia/platform
#   - source: corp/overlay
#     via: tamias-ref
```

`source` is an opaque locator — its grammar belongs to the resolver
(`via` names the scheme; absent/`tamias-ref` = the ambient tamias
resolver). An unknown `via` is a resolution error, never a silent
fallback. See [Composition](#composition) below.

### `template.merge`

Optional composition rules as data (defaults shown above). The
**installing (root) pack's** `merge` governs the whole chain —
ancestor packs' own `merge` tables describe how they compose when
installed directly.

* `vars` — pack-default precedence across the chain:
  `child-wins` (default, nearer packs win) or `parent-wins`.
* `into` — duplicate-target policy: `child-wins` (default, last
  render kept), `parent-wins` (first kept), or `error`.
* `max-depth` — ancestor-nesting cap (default 8, must be ≥ 1).

## Composition (`extends` chains)

A pack may inherit from other template packs. `tamias install`
resolves `template.extends` and materializes each ancestor's payload
inside the child's — `.scarab-parent/` for a single parent,
`.scarab-parents/<i>/` (index = declaration order) for several —
recursively, so a grandparent lands nested inside its parent.

The driver evaluates the chain **ancestor-first** (the agnostic
contract lives in `scarab-template`'s `compose.rs` +
`COMPOSITION.md`):

* parents render in declaration order, each parent's own ancestors
  before it; a shared ancestor renders **once** at its first
  occurrence (diamonds collapse)
* ancestor `template.vars` fold into the defaults ancestor-first —
  subject to `merge.vars`; the child's defaults then win under the
  default `child-wins`
* every chain entry's `files[]` renders against the one context;
  `into` conflicts resolve per `merge.into` (default: the
  descendant's render wins)
* the state file records only the final written digest per `into` —
  exactly what `uninstall` needs

Edge cases:

* materialized `.scarab-parent*/` present **without** `extends` is
  honored as vendored composition — useful for local packs and tests
* `extends` declared but fewer/more materialized parents than
  declared is an error: the payload never went through `tamias
  install` (or the layout is corrupt), and the driver can't fetch
  refs
* `extends: []` or a parent with an empty `source` fails manifest
  validation

## `TemplateEngine`

The engine port — one impl per syntax family:

```rust
pub trait TemplateEngine: Send + Sync {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
    fn render(&self, source: &str, ctx: &serde_json::Value)
        -> Result<String, Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>>;
}
```

`ctx` is a JSON object; engines map it to their native value.
`MinijinjaEngine` (`scarab-template-minijinja`) is the v1 impl —
sandboxed, keeps the template's trailing newline so rendered config
files stay POSIX-clean.

## Variable context

`merge_context(defaults, auto, file, args)` merges flat
`name → JSON value` layers, later winning:

```
ancestor template.vars … this pack's template.vars
    <  auto vars  <  --config file  <  env+args
```

On an `extends` chain the driver folds every ancestor's
`template.vars` into `defaults` ancestor-first, so nearer packs win.
The driver supplies the layers:

1. `template.vars` pack defaults — every ancestor's folded
   ancestor-first, then this pack's (nearest wins)
2. auto vars — `repo` (git `remote.origin.url` basename of the target
   dir, else canonical dir name) and `user` (`$USER`/`$LOGNAME`)
3. `--config` file — JSON by `.json`, TOML by `.toml`, YAML otherwise
   (incl. extensionless); must be a flat map
4. `$TEMPLATE_VAR_<NAME>` env vars, name lowercased, value parsed as
   JSON falling back to string
5. trailing `key=value` args — value parsed as JSON, falling back to
   string

## Errors

| Variant        | Meaning                                            |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `Manifest`     | Pack manifest or `template:` table failed to parse |
| `UnsafeTarget` | `into` escaped the deploy dir                      |
| `UnsafeSource` | `src` escaped the payload root                     |
| `NotUtf8`      | Rendered output isn't valid UTF-8 text             |

---

---
url: /scarab/reference/driver.md
---
# Template driver

`tamias-driver-template` is the tamias content driver for
`type: template` packs — it renders a pack's files into declared
targets. Discovered by tamias as `tamias-driver-template` on
`PATH`/`drivers/` like every content driver.

## argv contract

Tamias verbs always arrive as:

```
tamias-driver-template <verb> --dir <payload> --name <pkg> \
    [--config <vars-file>] [--target <dir>] [--dry-run] [key=value …]
```

| Flag        | Meaning                                                                                  |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--dir`     | Pack payload dir (contains `tamias.yaml`/`.yml`) — required for install/deploy/uninstall |
| `--name`    | Package name — required for install/deploy/uninstall                                     |
| `--config`  | Vars file — JSON/TOML/YAML by extension, YAML default                                    |
| `--target`  | Deploy target dir — overrides `$TEMPLATE_TARGET` and cwd                                 |
| `--dry-run` | Print actions without writing (deploy/uninstall)                                         |
| `key=value` | Trailing var overrides, highest-precedence layer                                         |

## Verbs

| Verb            | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                           | Exit      |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `install`       | Validate the pack *chain* (each manifest parses, every `src` compiles, vars resolve); print the merged render plan. Writes nothing — the payload dir is the evictable fetch cache. | 0 / 1 / 2 |
| `deploy`        | Render each `template.files[]` entry across the whole `extends` chain (ancestors first — the child wins on `into` conflicts), write at `into` under target dir, record state.      | 0 / 1 / 2 |
| `uninstall`     | Remove files still matching recorded sha256 digests; modified files kept + reported.                                                                                               | 0 / 1 / 2 |
| `config-schema` | Print JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for the `--config` vars file — a flat `name = value` map.                                                                                        | 0         |
| `capabilities`  | Print `{"name": "template", "types": ["template"], "verbs": ["install","deploy","uninstall","config-schema"], "engine": "minijinja"}`.                                             | 0         |

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` operational error (message on stderr —
tamias wraps it as `driver … failed: …`), `2` usage/arg error.

## `extends` chains

`install` and `deploy` walk the pack's chain: each level's payload
may nest its parents at `.scarab-parent/` (one parent) or
`.scarab-parents/<i>/` (several, index = declaration order) —
materialized by `tamias install` from `template.extends`.
`uninstall` needs no chain — it reverses whatever the state file
recorded.

* `install` reports the merged plan — every pack's `into`s in render
  order, with a count of files overridden by a later pack
* `deploy` renders ancestor-first under the root pack's
  `template.merge` rules; on an `into` conflict the default
  `child-wins` policy lets the child (later pack) write last and
  its digest is what state records
* `extends` declared but the materialized parent count doesn't
  match → error ("install through `tamias install`");
  `.scarab-parent*/` present without `extends` → honored as
  vendored parents
* var layers fold ancestor `template.vars` first (subject to
  `merge.vars`), so nearer packs win by default — see
  [template packs](/reference/template-packs#composition)

## State file

`deploy` writes `.scarab-template-state.json` at the target root:

```json
{
  "pack": "repo-bootstrap",
  "files": {
    "config/app.toml": "<sha256 hex>",
    "docs/NOTES.md": "<sha256 hex>"
  }
}
```

The file is shared per target dir — `deploy` merges its entries into
any existing state (multiple packs can coexist). `uninstall` removes
entries as files are deleted or found missing; the state file itself
is removed once `files` is empty.

## Driver errors

All failures surface as `OpsError` — a readable message on stderr:

* missing `--dir`/manifest, `type` isn't `"template"`, empty
  `template.files`, bad `template:` table shape
* unsafe `src`/`into` paths (rejected before any write)
* missing/unreadable payload files, render failures
* malformed `--config` vars file (must parse to a map)
* I/O errors on read/write/remove

---
url: /scarab/reference/testkit.md
---
# Testkit

`scarab-testkit` is the behavioral backbone for the config ports:
conformance suites any implementation runs to prove itself, plus
committed golden fixtures. Same pattern as `sepia-testkit` /
`tamias-testkit`. Dev-dependency only — it never ships in a
consumer's binary.

```toml
[dev-dependencies]
scarab-testkit = { git = "ssh://git@github.com/9aia/scarab.git" }
```

## Format conformance

`assert_config_format_conformance(format, &FormatCase)` checks a
\[`ConfigFormat`] against one scenario:

* extensions are claimed, non-empty, and unique
* `parse(text)` produces `expected`
* `render(expected)` re-parses to `expected` (round-trip)
* every `bad_inputs` entry fails with `Err` — never a panic

```rust
use scarab_config_yaml::YamlFormat;
use scarab_testkit::{FormatCase, assert_config_format_conformance};

assert_config_format_conformance(
    &YamlFormat,
    &FormatCase::new("app.yaml", "name: app\nport: 8080\n", cfg)
        .bad(["name: [unclosed"]),
);
```

## Discovery conformance

`assert_discovery_conformance(&case, make)` scripts a whole
filesystem + env scenario into a temp dir — files, search dirs,
env vars (paths resolve against the case root), an optional
explicit path — then runs `load_with_env` on whatever source `make`
builds from the \[`PreparedCase`]. The env lookup is injected; the
process environment is never touched.

```rust
use scarab_testkit::{DiscoveryCase, assert_discovery_conformance};

let case = DiscoveryCase::loaded("yaml beats toml", expected)
    .file("myapp.toml", "name = \"toml\"\n")
    .file("myapp.yaml", "name: yaml\n")
    .dir(".");
assert_discovery_conformance(&case, |pc| FileSource::new(
    Discovery::bare("myapp").dirs(pc.dirs().to_vec()),
));
```

`DiscoveryCase::error(name, needle)` expects a failure whose message
contains `needle`. Works for `FileSource`, `LayeredFileSource`, and
any future source implementing \[`EnvAwareSource`] (`load_with_env`).

## Source contract

For sources needing no injected env:
`assert_config_source_conformance(source, &expected)` and
`assert_config_source_error(source, "needle")` cover the minimal
\[`ConfigSource`] contract.

## Merge conformance

The pure half of layered loading — run once against
`scarab_config::{merge_value, apply_overrides}` themselves, or
against your own merge impl:

* `assert_merge_value_conformance(&[MergeCase])` — objects merge
  key-wise recursively; scalars/arrays/null replace; arrays never
  concatenate
* `assert_apply_overrides_conformance(&[OverrideCase])` — dotted-path
  leaves set in place, intermediate objects materialized

## Template engine conformance

`assert_template_engine_conformance(engine, &[TemplateCase])` is
engine-agnostic — cases carry source + JSON context + expected
output *or* expected error; only success/failure is contracted,
never error text. `TemplateCase::output` / `::error` build cases;
`assert_template_renders(engine, src, ctx, expected)` is the
one-off assertion.

## Fixtures and the canonical model

* `fixture_path(rel)` / `fixture_text(rel)` — committed golden files
  under `scarab-testkit/fixtures/` (`app.yaml`, `app.toml`,
  `layered/…`)
* `TestConfig` / `ServerConfig` — the canonical model the fixtures
  describe; reuse it, or define your own and reuse the `assert_*`
  suites unchanged

The suites panic on the first violated check — they're test helpers,
not libraries. `scarab-testkit`'s own `tests/conformance.rs` runs
every suite against the workspace impls and is the worked example.

* [Decisions](decisions.md) — ADR-lite: decision → alternative → consequence

url: /scarab/explanation/architecture.md

# Architecture

Scarab is ports-and-adapters in two planes: **config loading** and
**templated content**. Both are generic — scarab never names a
consumer's types.

## The config plane

```
ConfigSource<T>  ──load()──▶  T            (the port)
      ▲                            ▲
      │ impl                       │ consumer's serde model
scarab-config-file          MyConfig, TamiasConfig, …
      │ dispatches by extension
ConfigFormat<T>  ──parse/render──▶  text   (syntax port)
      ▲
scarab-config-toml / scarab-config-yaml
```

* `scarab-config` is pure: traits, the `Discovery` spec, path
  helpers, and the JSON merge half (`merge_value` /
  `apply_overrides`) — no I/O, no formats, no models.
* `scarab-config-file` is the discovery impl every org repo
  copy-pasted: `FileSource` picks the *first* matching file;
  `LayeredFileSource` merges *every* dir's file plus explicit/override
  layers into one `T`. Both dispatch by extension across a format
  list.
* `scarab-config-toml` / `-yaml` own only syntax — serde
  parse/render over any `T`. Formats are separate crates so a
  consumer can carry just the syntax it wants. Layered loading parses
  each layer as `serde_json::Value` through the same blanket impls,
  so `T` itself never needs `Serialize`.

Generic-over-`T` is the load-bearing decision: one `FileSource`
serves `myco`, `tamias`, `tarsi`, and every future repo because the
model stays in the consumer. The trait objects (`&dyn
ConfigFormat<T>`) keep `formats` heterogeneous without generics
exploding at the call site.

Discovery is a *spec*, not a search loop — `FileSource` interprets
it, and env/remote `ConfigSource` impls can reuse the same
vocabulary (`env_var`, `dirs`, preference order) without inheriting
file semantics.

## The template plane

```
tamias pack (type: template)
      │  tamias.yaml `template:` table
      ▼
scarab-template ── PackTemplate/TemplateFile/TemplateEngine (pure)
      │
      ▼
tamias-driver-template ── verbs, vars, state file (the ops impl)
      │
      ▼
scarab-template-minijinja ── the one engine impl (v1)
```

* `scarab-template` holds the pack model and path safety — pure
  domain, engine-agnostic. `merge_context` defines layer precedence;
  `safe_into`/`safe_src` define what "inside the target" means.
  `template.extends` composes packs: tamias materializes each
  ancestor's payload at `.scarab-parent/` (one parent) or
  `.scarab-parents/<i>/` (several), and the driver renders the
  chain ancestor-first under the root pack's `template.merge`
  rules — inheritance without a fetch capability in the driver.
* `tamias-driver-template` is where I/O lives: manifest loading,
  chain walking, var resolution (ancestor defaults → pack defaults
  → auto → file → env → args), render+write, digest state. It
  implements the tamias driver contract, so packs distribute through
  tamias like every other content type — no bespoke install path.
* `scarab-template-minijinja` is deliberately the only engine:
  minijinja is small, sandboxed by construction, and its
  `{{ }}`/`{% %}` syntax covers config-file templating without a
  plugin system. The port exists so a second syntax family can land
  without touching the model or the driver.

## Why the split

Config and templates share a shape — *declared inputs in, files
out* — but not a mechanism. Config is *read*: find a file, parse to
a typed model. Templates are *write*: render declared sources to
declared targets with a variable context. Keeping them as separate
ports means a consumer can adopt one without the other, and each
plane's invariants (discovery order vs. path safety + digest
state) stay local.

## Invariants worth knowing

* **Formats prefer YAML.** Within a directory, `yaml` → `yml` →
  `toml`; across dirs, earlier dirs win regardless of format.
* **Named paths fail loudly.** An explicit/`$*_CONFIG` path that
  misses is an error; discovery candidates skip silently.
* **Templates can't escape.** `..`/absolute/empty targets are
  rejected at validation, before any write.
* **Uninstall is digest-exact.** Only files still matching their
  recorded sha256 are removed; user edits are preserved and
  reported.
* **Layers merge as JSON, not as `T`.** `LayeredFileSource` folds
  `serde_json::Value` trees — objects key-wise, scalars/arrays
  replace — before one final deserialize, so merge semantics stay
  format- and model-agnostic.
* **Secrets stay names.** Config surfaces carry secret *names*,
  never values — cuora owns the values.

## Where it sits

Scarab is a **library** in the org's layering — delivery-layer
expertise consumed through tamias. The stack is **delivery**
(tamias distribution, scarab config/templates, tarsi releases,
bupha CI, hypha entity sync) → **memory** (myco, kuda) →
**process** (sturn, cuora, mimus, cicada, lasius, sepia,
peregrin) → **interface** (pavo).

Scarab doesn't run anywhere itself: organisms call `scarab-config`
to load their `<name>.yaml`/`.toml`, and tamias distributes
`type: template` packs that `tamias-driver-template` renders. It
sits beneath the layers as shared expertise — the config port every
organism agrees on, the template mechanism every pack shares.

---

---
url: /scarab/explanation/concepts.md
---
# Concepts

The domain vocabulary, each term defined once. Field-level contracts
live in [Reference](../reference/).

## ConfigSource / ConfigFormat

The two config-plane traits. `ConfigSource<T>` finds and loads a `T`
(one `load()`); `ConfigFormat<T>` owns one syntax — serde
parse/render over text, dispatched by file extension. Both are
generic over the consumer's model: scarab never names a `Config`
type. See [Architecture](architecture.md#the-config-plane).

## Discovery

The spec, not the search loop: `env_var`, `dirs`, format preference,
explicit-path handling. `FileSource` interprets it for the
filesystem; other `ConfigSource` impls can reuse the same vocabulary.
`Discovery::for_app(name)` wires the org conventions —
`$<NAME>_CONFIG`, `[".", "~/.config/<name>"]`, YAML preferred.

## Layered loading

`LayeredFileSource` merges one file *per* search dir plus
explicit/override layers — JSON-value merge (objects key-wise,
scalars/arrays replace) before one final deserialize — so user
config is the base and project config lands on top. Contrast
`FileSource`, which takes the *first* match.

## Template pack

A tamias package of `type: template`: a `template:` table in
`tamias.yaml` declaring sources, targets (`into`), variables,
optional `extends` parents, and `merge` rules. Packs are ordinary
tamias content — installed, deployed, and uninstalled by
`tamias-driver-template`. See [Reference: template
packs](../reference/template-packs).

## TemplateEngine

The render port: `{{ }}` vars + `{% %}` blocks over a context.
`scarab-template-minijinja` is the only v1 impl — sandboxed by
construction, no filesystem or network reach.

## merge_context

Layer precedence for template variables: ancestor defaults → pack
defaults → auto → file → env → args. Defined once in
`scarab-template` so every driver agrees.

## Path safety

`safe_into`/`safe_src`: targets and sources must stay inside the
pack/target roots — `..`, absolute, and empty paths are rejected at
validation, before any write.

## Digest state

The driver's record of what it wrote (sha256 per file). Uninstall is
exact: only files still matching their digest are removed; user
edits survive and are reported.

## Secret names, never values

Config surfaces and template vars carry secret *names* (or
references); [cuora](https://9aia.com/cuora/) owns resolution. This
is a convention the whole org enforces — see
[Boundaries](boundaries.md).

---

---
url: /scarab/explanation/boundaries.md
---
# Boundaries

Scarab owns two things: **config loading** (discovery + formats,
generic over the model) and **templated content packs** (the
`type: template` driver). Everything adjacent belongs to a neighbor.

## Neighbors

| Repo                        | Owns                                                                         | Scarab's relation                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **tamias**                  | Content distribution — refs, fetch, store, install pipeline, driver dispatch | Scarab ships *inside* tamias's world: `tamias-driver-template` is a content driver; template packs are tamias packages. Scarab never reimplements fetch/install/store. |
| **cuora**                   | Secret values — sealed, not spilled                                          | Config carries secret *names*, never values. A template var named `api_key` holds a reference/name; cuora resolves it.                                                 |
| **tarsi**                   | Release plane — changelog → bump → tag → publish                             | A consumer: `tarsi.toml`/profile loading rides `scarab-config`.                                                                                                        |
| **myco / kuda / mimus**     | Work ledger, code-map, verification                                          | Consumers of the config port for their own `<name>.yaml`/`.toml` discovery — the exact problem P-017 generalized.                                                      |
| **hypha**                   | Pure distributed substrate                                                   | The P-015 config crates were ported *here*, not kept there — hypha stays substrate-only.                                                                               |
| **peregrin / sepia / pavo** | Orchestration, sessions, agent UI                                            | May consume either plane; neither defines scarab's contracts.                                                                                                          |

## What scarab deliberately is not

* **Not a config schema registry.** It loads and renders; it doesn't
  validate semantics. Your serde model *is* the schema.
* **Not a secrets store.** See cuora above — the boundary is
  enforced by convention (`secret names, never values`) and by
  cuora owning resolution.
* **Not a template marketplace.** Packs are ordinary tamias
  packages; distribution, provenance, and digests are tamias's
  job.
* **Not consumer-aware.** No crate in scarab may name another
  repo's `Config` type — that coupling is what the port exists to
  prevent.

## The naming story

*Scarabaeus sacer* — the sacred scarab rolls the ball into place;
scarab amulets were seals and signets. Config as the seal that
validates what runs: discovery finds the right file, the format
parses it, the model validates it. Design history lives in the org
ledger — proposal P-017 (supersedes P-015).

---

---
url: /scarab/explanation/decisions.md
---
# Decisions

ADR-lite: the load-bearing decisions, each with the alternative it
beat and the consequence it carries. Design history lives in the
org ledger — proposal P-017 (supersedes P-015).

## Generic over `T`, never a consumer's model

**Decision:** `ConfigSource<T>`/`ConfigFormat<T>` are generic over
the consumer's serde model — scarab never names a `Config` type.

* *Alternative:* a scarab-owned universal config schema.
* *Consequence:* one `FileSource` serves myco, tamias, tarsi, and
  every future repo; each consumer keeps only its serde model. Cost:
  trait objects at the call site to keep generics from exploding.

## Discovery is a spec, not a search loop

**Decision:** `Discovery` declares `env_var`, `dirs`, format
preference, explicit-path handling; `FileSource` interprets it.

* *Alternative:* hard-coded per-repo search logic (the
  `gen-*.py`/copy-paste status quo).
* *Consequence:* env/remote `ConfigSource` impls reuse the same
  vocabulary without inheriting file semantics.

## Formats are separate crates

**Decision:** `scarab-config-toml` and `-yaml` own only syntax;
`scarab-config` stays pure (traits, `Discovery`, merge helpers).

* *Alternative:* one crate with all formats baked in.
* *Consequence:* a consumer carries just the syntax it wants; the
  port stays I/O-free and unit-testable.

## Config and templates are separate planes

**Decision:** config is *read* (find, parse, model); templates are
*write* (render sources to targets with a var context) — two ports,
two invariants.

* *Alternative:* one unified "content" port.
* *Consequence:* a consumer adopts one plane without the other;
  discovery order vs. path-safety+digest invariants stay local.

## MiniJinja is the only engine (v1)

**Decision:** `scarab-template-minijinja` is deliberately the sole
`TemplateEngine` impl — sandboxed by construction.

* *Alternative:* a plugin system for template syntax.
* *Consequence:* `{{ }}`/`{% %}` covers config-file templating
  without attack surface; the port exists so a second syntax family
  can land without touching model or driver.

## Uninstall is digest-exact

**Decision:** the driver records sha256 per written file;
uninstall removes only files still matching.

* *Alternative:* remove everything the pack declared.
* *Consequence:* user edits survive uninstall and are reported —
  templated files are owned only until touched.

## Secrets stay names

**Decision:** config surfaces and template vars carry secret
*names*, never values; cuora owns resolution.

* *Alternative:* templated secret injection.
* *Consequence:* packs are safe to distribute and review; the
  boundary is convention plus cuora owning the values.
